arxiv-1811-11033.title: Reconstruction of intermittent data time series as a superposition of pulses
arxiv-1811-11033.creator: Sajidah Ahmed, Odd Erik Garcia, Audun Theodorsen
arxiv-1811-11033.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Sajidah Ahmed, Odd Erik Garcia, Audun Theodorsen. Fluctuations in a vast range of physical systems can be described as a superposition of uncorrelated pulses with a fixed shape, a process commonly referred to as a (generalized) shot noise or a filtered Poisson process. In this contribution, we present a systematic study of a novel deconvolution method to estimate the arrival times and amplitudes of the pulses from realizations of such processes.

arxiv-1904-00296.title: Using Scratch to Teach Undergraduate Students’ Skills on Artificial Intelligence
arxiv-1904-00296.creator: Julian Estevez, Gorka Garate, JM Lopez-Guede, Manuel Graña
arxiv-1904-00296.description: Abstract This paper presents a educational workshop in Scratch that is proposed for the active participation of undergraduate students in contexts of Artificial Intelligence. The main objective of the activity is to demystify the complexity of Artificial Intelligence and its algorithms. For this purpose, students must realize simple exercises of clustering and two neural networks, in Scratch.

arxiv-2306-15031.title: On the Required Secure Key Rate for Quantum-Secured Optical Channels
arxiv-2306-15031.description: Abstract The current maturity of the quantum-secured optical data channels based on the Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) technology is at the deployment level in metro environments, while R&D efforts are also being conducted towards long-distance deployments. A great deal of research has been conducted on the achievable Secure Key Rate (SKR) for quantum channels.

arxiv-2502-01322.creator: Mohammed Sabbah, Robbie Mears, Leah R. Murphy, Kerrianne Harrington, James M. Stone, Tim A. Birks, John C. Travers
arxiv-2502-01322.description: Abstract Tunable ultrashort laser pulses across the near-ultraviolet to near-infrared with high peak power are crucial for wide-ranging applications in science and industry. Resonant dispersive-wave emission in gas-filled hollow-core fibers is a well-established technique for generating tunable ultrashort pulses from the vacuum ultraviolet to the near-infrared.

arxiv-2504-09610.title: Q-ball mechanism of electron transport and spin/lattice excitations properties of high-T c superconductors
arxiv-2504-09610.creator: S. I. Mukhin
arxiv-2504-09610.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by S. I. Mukhin. In this work the Q-ball mechanism of high-Tc superconductivity in cuprates, recently proposed by the author, is applied to explanation of the electron and spin/lattice properties found experimentally. Euclidean Q-balls (nontopological solitons) are Bose condensed collective spin/charge density wave fluctuations (SDW/CDW) with zero static mean that arise inside a Q-ball volume simultaneously with Cooper/local pairs superconducting condensate for which they serve as the ’pairing glue’.

arxiv-2509-01093.title: Natural Context Drift Undermines the Natural Language Understanding of Large Language Models
arxiv-2509-01093.creator: Yulong Wu, Viktor Schlegel, Riza Batista-Navarro
arxiv-2509-01093.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yulong Wu, Viktor Schlegel, Riza Batista-Navarro. How does the natural evolution of context paragraphs affect question answering in generative Large Language Models (LLMs)? To investigate this, we propose a framework for curating naturally evolved, human-edited variants of reading passages from contemporary QA benchmarks and for analyzing LLM performance across a range of semantic similarity scores, which quantify how closely each variant aligns with content seen during pretraining. Using this framework, we evaluate six QA datasets and eight LLMs with publicly available training data.

pmc-10741399.title: Research on Teleoperated Virtual Reality Human–Robot Five-Dimensional Collaboration System
pmc-10741399.creator: Qinglei Zhang, Qinghao Liu, Jianguo Duan, Jiyun Qin, Pengcheng Liu, Qinbing Fu, Tiong Hoo Lim
pmc-10741399.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In the realm of industrial robotics, there is a growing challenge in simplifying human–robot collaboration (HRC), particularly in complex settings. The demand for more intuitive teleoperation systems is on the rise. However, optimizing robot control interfaces and streamlining teleoperation remains a formidable task due to the need for operators to possess specialized knowledge and the limitations of traditional methods regarding operational space and time constraints. This study addresses these issues by introducing a virtual reality (VR) HRC system with five-dimensional capabilities.

pmc-11484569.title: Combination Doxycycline and Topical Corticosteroids in the Treatment of Ulcerative Pyoderma Gangrenosum: A Case Report
pmc-11484569.creator: Doha Mae Laurisse M. Manalo-Legas, Erickah Mary Therese D. Calayag, Eillen Luisa A. Chen
pmc-11484569.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Pyoderma gangrenosum (PG) is a chronic inflammatory neutrophilic dermatosis often presenting as a solitary enlarging painful ulcer with red to violaceous undermined borders. This report delves into the role of doxycycline in the treatment of PG in a 44-year-old male COVID-19 positive patient who has concomitant active tuberculosis infection and end-stage kidney disease, for which both first-line treatments (systemic corticosteroid and cyclosporine) are contraindicated.

In particular, this paper focuses on providing a research model to analyze the behavior towards the use of interactive digital whiteboards (IDWs) by teachers in the educational context, highlighting their impact on the intention to use IDWS.

INTRODUCTION

Over the past decade, the field of biotherapies has made remarkable progress in treating diseases using genetic modification. Genetic modification components (e.g., viral vectors) can be administered directly to the patient (in vivo) or cells can be collected, modified externally, and reinfused (ex vivo). Gene delivery and editing techniques have advanced over time to meet the practical and functional needs of manufacturing cellular therapies.
